description:
FILED s483b (Opus, 2026-09-13), found by the #1618 probe battery (a probe file
whose EARLIER rows answered wrongly because of text FURTHER DOWN).
PRE-EXISTING on main e3767cff -- verified byte-identical there.

A variable holding a CODE REF is given the `:str` raw-slot verdict and the
code ref is STRINGIFIED INTO THE SLOT at its declaration:

    (p-let (($cr :str (%pcl-to-string-strict <the lambda> "$cr") :captured t))

After that every use of $cr sees the string "CODE(0x...)": `$cr->[i]` and
`@$cr` become SYMBOLIC array derefs (undef / empty instead of perl's fatal),
and `$cr->()` dies "Undefined subroutine &main::CODE(0x...)".  The value is
gone -- the #138 silent-wrong family, at run time.

THE DISCRIMINATOR IS ONE TOKEN (both files below transpile, both run):

  A (wrong)                                    B (right)
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  sub T { my ($n, $c) = @_; my $v = eval { $c->() };
          my $e = $@; $e =~ s/ at .*//s;
          print "$n: ", (defined $v ? "[$v]" : "undef"), " err=[$e]\n"; }

  my $cr = sub { 7 };
  T "30 cr->[1]"   => sub { my $x = $cr->[1]; ref($x) || "$x" };
  T "36 \@\$cr"    => sub { ... };     T "36 at-dollar-cr" => sub { ... };
                     ^^^^^^^^^^ the only difference: an ESCAPED \$cr in a
                     double-quoted LABEL, which is not a use of $cr at all

    perl (both):   30 ... undef err=[Not an ARRAY reference]
                   36 ... undef err=[Not an ARRAY reference]
    PCL A:         30 ... [] err=[]        36 ... [0] err=[]
    PCL B:         identical to perl
    PCL A with PCL_NO_RAW_VERDICT=1:  identical to perl

So the raw-verdict scanner counts `\$cr` INSIDE A STRING (backslash-escaped,
i.e. a literal `$cr` in the output, NOT an interpolation) as a string-typed
USE of the variable, and the other uses in the file (`$cr->[i]`, `@$cr`) do
not veto `:str` because a string is a legal operand there (a symbolic ref).
An escaped `\$` must not register a variable use at all.

Probe files kept: scratch/s483b/probes/bx4.pl (A), bx12.pl (B), and
b1618b.pl, whose rows 30-39/44/50 are all this one bug.

BAR: the scanner must ignore `\$name` / `\@name` in a dq string (grep the
sibling readers -- Pl::InterpScan is the ONE scanner, standing rule);
~10 probes vs perl including the ones that must NOT change (a real
interpolation `"$cr"` DOES make it a string use; `'single \$cr'`; `\\$cr`,
which IS an interpolation preceded by a literal backslash), a guard row,
inverse-verified, plus a corpus-diff (this is an emission verdict, so a
generation bump and the emission-ab legs apply).
SIZE: M.

=== DONE (s483c) ===
FIX: the escape rule is `Pl::InterpScan::escape_skip`, extracted out of
`scan`'s driver loop (byte-identical there) and walked by
`Pl::VarAnnotator::_tw_scan_quote_leaf`; a LITERAL heredoc (PPI's
`_mode eq 'literal'`) is not scanned at all.  A backslash hides the next
character, and in dq text `\cX` hides the X while in a PATTERN it does not â
one definition, per the Â§8 standing rule.

THE FINDING behind it: a `str` use is a LICENCE, not a conservative default.
It is what lets Parser2 wrap the write in `%pcl-to-string-strict` and keep a
host STRING in the slot, so over-firing does not "stay safe" â it DESTROYS
the value.  Same session, same commit, the hole from the other side: #1622
(a name CAPTURED by a nested anon sub has reads the walk never classifies).
`docs/raw-numeric-verdict.md` gained both rules as normative text.

MEASURED (the whole commit): corpus-diff IDENTICAL over 111 files + 6 shapes;
emission-ab vs 6eea8578 over 1034 files SAME=1034 DIFF=0 RCDIFF=0 â the fix
only ever REMOVES a freeze that no corpus file earned.  Guard rows 61-70 in
Pl/t/raw-verdict-01.t, INVERSE-verified on a 6eea8578 `git archive`
extraction (61-67 fail there; 68-70, the must-not-change side, pass on both).
One product site DOES lose a verdict â `cl/pack-impl.pl`'s `_unpack_str`
`$slen`, captured by an anon sub whose own read is licensing â at no
measurable cost; the precise fix is filed as #1629.
FULL sweep (perl tools/sweep-perl-tests.pl --jobs 4): GATE clean, 0 new / 0 fixed, TOTAL passing 18675 = baseline (+0), dropped statements census 5 / current 5 (+0).  The 5 UNSTABLE rows (method.t 2, magic.t 1, yadayada.t 2) are crash-file noise: method.t's fail SET is byte-identical between the base extraction and this tree (23 rows, 76 pass both).
FULL gate on the final rebased tree: 236 files / 8097 rows, failures ONLY xs-01/02/03 (the 13 standing pclxs rows) = green.  The base extraction is 235 files / 8091 with the new 70-row raw-verdict-01.t in place, i.e. 8081 + 10 + 6 = 8097 exactly.
subject: an ESCAPED \$name in a dq string counts as a string USE for the raw-slot verdict -- a CODE ref is stringified into its own slot and the value is LOST
